guards.name: test-layout
guards.invariant: To make test ownership discoverable, require each canonical test path to mirror its source or belong to a dedicated test tree.

guards.name: clock-single-source
guards.invariant: To keep time deterministic in tests, route all rebuild wall-clock and monotonic reads through the clock adapter.

guards.name: dashboard-design-rules
guards.invariant: To prevent dashboard design drift, enforce the shared type scale, palette, date formatting, used CSS, and semantic controls.

guards.name: dashboard-consistency
guards.invariant: To keep dashboard errors and dialogs consistent, forbid danger Banner or Notice errors and any dialog size beyond sm, md and lg.

guards.name: dashboard-wire-boundary
guards.invariant: To keep browser bundles portable and small, require schema-derived wire types, exclude Node built-ins and workflow definitions from browser entries, and keep operator code out of the design-system specimen.

guards.name: gate-coverage
guards.invariant: To prevent inert wrappers from passing the gate, require the configured typecheck, lint, coverage, and focused test commands to exercise their intended inputs.

guards.name: guard-manifest
guards.invariant: To catch unregistered or orphaned guards and skipped tests, reconcile guard files, Vitest project ownership, coverage policy, and required scanners.

guards.name: dom-node-assertions
guards.invariant: To stop failed assertions from exhausting runner memory while formatting DOM nodes, forbid equality checks via node:assert on values containing those nodes.

guards.name: manual-clock-test-only
guards.invariant: To keep synthetic time out of production, restrict manualClock access to tests.

guards.name: src-imports-no-tests
guards.invariant: To keep mocks and test fixtures out of the served app, forbid production modules from importing or re-exporting them.

guards.name: settings-catalog
guards.invariant: To keep configuration legal and traceable, reconcile runtime settings with their sensitivity, authority, and channel in the closed catalog.

guards.name: no-secret-values-in-logs
guards.invariant: To prevent credential disclosure, reject raw credential interpolation in logs and require reviewed display boundaries for local identifiers.

guards.name: terminal-failures
guards.invariant: To make terminal failures visible, require request and asynchronous failure paths to preserve refusals and diagnostics.

guards.name: operational-isolation
guards.invariant: To prevent runtimes from colliding, give each configured runtime distinct state, ports, locks, and browser profiles.

guards.name: operator-mutation-admission
guards.invariant: To restrict operator writes to the local authorized client, register each browser-reachable mutation with admission and loopback Host and Origin checks.

guards.name: runtime-dependency-coverage
guards.invariant: To catch missing or test-only runtime dependencies, reconcile production browser and provider declarations with their capabilities, endpoint checks, and credentials.

guards.name: runtime-environment-coverage
guards.invariant: To prevent hidden configuration channels, classify every environment read and explicitly refuse retired configuration keys.

guards.name: secrets-single-source
guards.invariant: To prevent credential access from spreading through runtime code, confine provider secret reads to the canonical secrets module.

guards.name: build-id-roots
guards.invariant: To invalidate stale workers after source changes, hash all worker-runnable source and prevent it from loading dashboard code.

guards.name: strict-boundary-schemas
guards.invariant: To reject malformed external or durable data, require schema-derived boundaries that refuse nested unknown keys and unsafe parser escapes.

guards.name: test-runtime-root-isolation
guards.invariant: To protect real runtime state during tests, forbid test writes to configured state, artifact, lock, and browser-profile roots.

guards.name: test-target-registry
guards.invariant: To keep operator and test inputs distinct, require a frozen target registry with exact workflow ownership, availability, and input classification.

guards.name: test-data-ownership
guards.invariant: To prevent fixtures from leaking across tiers or causing runtime effects at import, keep unit-only data local and put shared fixtures under their consumer owners.

guards.name: artifact-effect-boundary
guards.invariant: To keep artifact paths private and writes complete, expose immutable artifact references and publish through verified isolated storage.

guards.name: atomic-write-outbox
guards.invariant: To prevent partial write settlement, commit the operation, attempt, checkpoint, and confirmation event in one authority transaction.

guards.name: bounded-task-deadline
guards.invariant: To prevent stalled tasks from holding workers indefinitely, arm every task invocation with a mandatory abortable deadline.

guards.name: store-reading-timers
guards.invariant: To keep repeating store reads off idle request paths, require review of backend timers that repeatedly read stores.

guards.name: failure-code-catalog
guards.invariant: To keep operator failure messages descriptive, register every failure code declared by a task contract.

guards.name: canonical-input-snapshot
guards.invariant: To preserve admitted inputs across replay, require transform-free canonical schemas and reject corrupted snapshots or incompatible schema hashes.

guards.name: ocr-proof-boundaries
guards.invariant: To prevent OCR writes or retries from escaping their scope, bind each command, review edit, and retry to its native owner and proof.

guards.name: control-command-single-path
guards.invariant: To prevent replay or mutation through alternate command paths, bind roster audit reads to original command results and centralize journal and audit writes.

guards.name: delegation-manifest
guards.invariant: To prevent delegation replay drift, require a shared edge policy and fingerprint the edge, cardinality, join, policy, and every child input.

guards.name: descriptor-coverage
guards.invariant: To keep workflow registries and consumers aligned, reconcile descriptor identities, contracts, examples, and derived browser systems.

guards.name: driver-lease-boundary
guards.invariant: To prevent browser driver access outside session ownership, acquire drivers only through the reviewed callback lease.

guards.name: evidence-receipt
guards.invariant: To make terminal results verifiable, require strict receipts with fingerprints, observed facts, verified write bindings, and explicit confidence.

guards.name: fresh-session-boundary
guards.invariant: To prevent unintended browser-session reuse, require authored or identity-forced fresh-session boundaries.

guards.name: identity-gate-before-commit
guards.invariant: To prevent separation writes or results from bypassing identity approval, require every dependency path from a transaction or terminal result to reach the operator gate.

guards.name: no-lifecycle-sql-outside-the-adapter
guards.invariant: To prevent competing lifecycle writers, confine lifecycle mutations to reviewed SQLite and run-service owners.

guards.name: no-positional-identity
guards.invariant: To keep durable records stable across reorder or replay, reject positional and borrowed identities.

guards.name: one-projection-counts
guards.invariant: To keep dashboard and queue counts consistent, derive workflow, status, queue, and month totals from the shared run projection.

guards.name: ucpath-person-org-strict
guards.invariant: To prevent UCPath from returning a false identity or not-found result, require the verified legacy lookup flow and exact employee identity.

guards.name: provider-capability-boundary
guards.invariant: To keep vendor calls bounded and auditable, give each capability one timeout and confine raw network dependencies to approved adapters.

guards.name: scenario-coverage
guards.invariant: To keep synthetic scenarios tied to the workflow graph, derive coverage points from nodes and reject stale, orphaned, or unexecuted claims.

guards.name: semantic-ui-registry
guards.invariant: To prevent ambiguous browser lookup across systems, require unique classified UI IDs, distinct search terms, and valid verification scenarios.

guards.name: single-flight-login
guards.invariant: To prevent duplicate login ceremonies, share a single in-flight login across concurrent leases for one worker and system.

guards.name: storage-recovery
guards.invariant: To protect authority during storage faults, verify immutable backups, degrade to read-only on failure, and keep restore offline.

guards.name: subject-before-fence
guards.invariant: To prevent writes against a changed subject, verify the prepared identity on the same lease before committing the fence and calling the mutation.

guards.name: workflow-failure-codes
guards.invariant: To give Explorer text for every intentional failure, audit authored workflow failure codes against canonical task contracts.

guards.name: task-contract-sealing
guards.invariant: To prevent malformed task definitions, mint read, prepare, and commit contracts only through the effect-aware validating factory.

guards.name: task-driver-boundary
guards.invariant: To prevent workflows from bypassing driver ownership, confine raw Playwright types, imports, and operations to the designated browser owners.

guards.name: task-store-boundaries
guards.invariant: To keep task access aligned with browser sessions, require one store and provider per system with matching driver, effect, and lease policies.

guards.name: transaction-pairing
guards.invariant: To make transaction writes attributable and bounded, pair prepare and commit under one system lease with a derived key, fence budget, and dry-run policy.

guards.name: explorer-prose-declared
guards.invariant: To keep Explorer consistent with authored workflows, serve each descriptor summary and each node purpose or timeline description from its declaration.

guards.name: wire-connectivity
guards.invariant: To keep dashboard requests aligned with backend support, reconcile advertised wire sections with implemented queries and reviewed pending bindings.

guards.name: write-safety-contract
guards.invariant: To recover external writes safely, require each commit contract to declare a proof schema, extractors, output reconstruction, and a same-store probe.

guards.name: authentication-proof-not-url
guards.invariant: To prevent false login success, require content-level authentication proof on every return path through a verified login recipe.

guards.name: intake-canonical-field-registry
guards.invariant: To keep intake fields grounded in actual documents, reconcile the canonical vocabulary with the recorded scan inventory in both directions.

guards.name: intake-mapping-boundary
guards.invariant: To prevent inferred mappings from becoming operator decisions, keep suggestions separate from confirmed bindings and validate persisted mappings.

guards.name: ocr-producer-parity
guards.invariant: To give every OCR source the same admission guarantees, validate provider, agent, and operator extractions through the same rules.

guards.name: redaction-surface-scan
guards.invariant: To prevent classified values from escaping approved surfaces, audit wire, storage, notification, and provider disclosures against their allowed custody.

guards.name: redaction-workbook-origins
guards.invariant: To prevent workbook values from escaping through metadata or actions, pin their classified origins to loopback or durable authority.

guards.name: redaction-worker-startup-origins
guards.invariant: To prevent startup errors from bypassing redaction, pin message and detail origins across the operator surfaces that share them.

guards.name: dashboard-refresh-boundary
guards.invariant: To keep dashboard edits compatible with React refresh, limit runtime exports of surface and app TSX modules to components.

guards.name: dashboard-memo-prop-stability
guards.invariant: To avoid unnecessary dashboard renders, require memoization and stable props for the workspace rail, queue, and logs.

guards.name: dashboard-presentation-inventory
guards.invariant: To catch unreviewed dashboard styling changes, pin the component, stylesheet, and token files that define its presentation.

guards.name: command-result-exhaustive
guards.invariant: To keep command refusals visible after schema changes, require exhaustive dashboard handling and keep transport inside its shared owners.

guards.name: workflow-structure
guards.invariant: To keep workflow ownership discoverable, require each workflow to compose its declared steps and keep task and step definitions in their designated directories.

guards.name: workflow-layout
guards.invariant: To keep the sources aligned with the workflow rail and timeline, require the folder tree to match registered workflow and step identities.

guards.name: no-workflow-id-branches
guards.invariant: To keep adding workflows independent of shared code, forbid workflow-ID literals in generic modules outside reviewed sites.

guards.name: duo-ceremony-lease
guards.invariant: To prevent concurrent ceremonies from invalidating a Duo credential, require an owner-issued lease before SSO or WebAuthn access.

guards.name: step-omission-invariants
guards.invariant: To preserve operator approval when a step is omitted, allow only that step to supply task facts, keep gates and transactions outside substitution, and skip them only where the step declares it.

guards.name: worker-loop-writes-only-through-the-service
guards.invariant: To prevent workers from bypassing lifecycle rules, keep lifecycle writes behind the service and reject direct or aliased repository mutations.

guards.name: rerun-prefill-boundary
guards.invariant: To keep copied values from granting replay authority, validate descriptor schema, source version, and value coordinates before admitting a new plan.

guards.name: composition-reads-no-environment-leaf
guards.invariant: To prevent ambient environment overrides, refuse retired keys before startup effects and keep raw reads out of configuration modules.

guards.name: test-artifact-ownership
guards.invariant: To keep generated test output out of source control, require ignored local artifacts, external scratch space, and an owner for accepted evidence.

guards.name: sqlite-authority-boundary
guards.invariant: To prevent callers from bypassing SQLite authority or stalling the BFF, keep raw SQL inside reviewed private adapters and hand dashboard debug appends to the log writer thread.

guards.name: start-plan-contract
guards.invariant: To prevent dashboard and server validation from drifting, share one strict start-plan wire schema with common defaults and refusals.

guards.name: synthetic-database-admission-boundary
guards.invariant: To keep synthetic runs faithful and isolated, reach real database admission through a narrow import boundary without test-data readers or app composition.

guards.name: admission-identity
guards.invariant: To prevent forged admission identities and initialization cycles, restrict issuance to the token-protected constructor and keep the audited RuntimeAdmission imports type-only.

guards.name: store-query-plan
guards.invariant: To keep dashboard and worker queries fast as history grows, require indexed access or reviewed bounds on scans and sorts.

guards.name: names-check
guards.invariant: To avoid wasting CI on invalid metadata, enforce allowed branch, worktree, and pull-request naming rules.

guards.name: allowed-workflows
guards.invariant: To keep ad hoc workflows from bypassing the shared CI pipeline, reject unapproved workflow files unless the pull request has the required review label.

repositoryChecks.name: span-task-namespace-parity
repositoryChecks.invariant: Reason: the persisted span task grammar omitted the existing workbooks namespace and rejected native workbook task observations. Require identical canonical and span task grammars, exercise every browser/service namespace, and refuse invalid namespaces and operations in both.

repositoryChecks.name: completed-restore-custody
repositoryChecks.invariant: Reason: settled restore suspects outlive their journal. Strict completed history binds exact profile/operation/file identities and complete companions before credential inventory. Unrelated registry mutations preserve that history, and interrupted publication settles once without accepting divergence.

repositoryChecks.name: public-repository-privacy
repositoryChecks.invariant: Private HR inputs and credentials must not enter the public tree. Inspect staged paths and textual blobs; allow only named synthetic documents and known synthetic tokens in reviewed example locations. Report paths and rules without values.
